transcript_header:
Date: 2026-02-18
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Tom Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Leon Wu (Redwood SE - backup), Mark Dalton (CTO, BlueHarbor), Sarah Nguyen (Head of ML), Olivia Park (Finance), Ethan Cole (Infra)
transcript:
[00:00] Tom Reyes: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Tom from Redwood, with Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Mark Dalton: Good, thanks Tom. Busy week but excited to dig in.
[00:09] Priya Kapoor: Great, quick agenda - we're here to understand your workload, budgets, and then walk through hosting options and cost levers — token pricing, batching, caching, dedicated sizing, that sort of thing.
[00:18] Sarah Nguyen: Yeah that's right. At BlueHarbor we've been prototyping chat assistants and document summarization. We're hitting cost surprises on our current provider, so main goal is to understand unit econ if we move to Redwood hosted or reserved/dedicated.
[00:28] Olivia Park: And from finance side, we need predictable monthly run-rate and options for caps.
[00:33] Tom Reyes: Totally, that makes sense. Could you give us a quick sense of your traffic profile — QPS, average tokens in, tokens out, and percent of streaming vs small single-turn calls?
[00:42] Sarah Nguyen: Sure. Right now peak QPS is about 6 across US clients, average request is about 120 prompt tokens and 180 response tokens. 20% are streaming multi-chunk responses for long-form summarization, rest are single-shot. Monthly active requests ~1.2M.
[00:58] Ethan Cole: Note we're running in AWS us-east and have some on-prem data for sensitive customers.
[01:03] Priya Kapoor: Okay, that profile helps a lot. So high-level: Hosted we price per token, with tiers and volume discounts; Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity with a monthly commit, so you get predictable throughput and lower per-token cost especially when you have sustained usage. Private/VPC is similar to Dedicated but with private control plane and extra enterprise fees.
[01:20] Mark Dalton: Can you put numbers on that — ballpark per-token delta between hosted and dedicated?
[01:24] Tom Reyes: Ballpark — for our curated open models, hosted might be in the range of $0.0006 to $0.002 per input+output token depending on model size and volume. Dedicated can bring effective per-token to something like $0.00015 to $0.0006 once you amortize the reserved capacity and get higher utilization. Those are rough, ymmv.
[01:44] Olivia Park: That's a big range. We need scenarios given our 1.2M monthly requests and your token sizes.
[01:49] Priya Kapoor: We'll build a cost scenario spreadsheet — we typically give Hosted cost projection side-by-side with a Dedicated commit scenario at different utilization levels: 40%, 60%, 80%. Important to include batching, kv/prefix caching and quantization — those are levers to reduce per-token compute.
[02:03] Sarah Nguyen: Quick question — how much does batching help for our traffic? We have shortish requests but maybe can batch at 50-150ms latency target.
[02:10] Priya Kapoor: Good question. With continuous batching, for small/median sequence lengths you can reduce per-token compute by 15-40% depending on QPS and latency SLO. If you can tolerate slightly higher tail latency we can push batching windows a bit. Also prefix/KV caching for repeated context, like system prompts or shared docs, can reduce generation tokens by up to 30% in some workloads.
[02:29] Mark Dalton: Any gotchas with caching? Data residency or security concerns?
[02:33] Tom Reyes: Caches are configurable per-tenant, and for Private deployments you get the cache data plane inside your VPC. We support encryption and KMS integration for any cached artifacts; retention policies can be set. There are tradeoffs — cache hit rate depends on prompt similarity.
[02:45] Ethan Cole: On quantization — do you support int8 / awq style? Does that affect quality for our summarization?
[02:50] Priya Kapoor: We recommend quantization profiles by model and workload. For many encoder-decoder or LLM models, int8/awq gives a good cost/quality tradeoff; we provide guidance and A/B evals. We'll run a quick eval on your sample prompts to quantify ROUGE/ROBOT metrics.
[03:04] Sarah Nguyen: Sounds good. We care about latency percentiles — p50 vs p95; what numbers can we expect on hosted vs dedicated?
[03:11] Tom Reyes: Hosted p50 for same model is typically 30-80ms per token depending on model size and region; p95 can be higher, and dedicated gives tighter SLOs because you control the pool. With reserved GPUs and prioritized scheduling you can hit better p95s, especially for high throughput. We'll surface token-level latency breakdowns in the console.
[03:27] Olivia Park: For procurement, what's the minimum committed spend for Dedicated?
[03:31] Tom Reyes: We commonly see monthly commitments starting around $8k-$15k depending on GPU mix; enterprise teams can negotiate multi-month terms. There's also burst/buffer capacity options for spiky traffic.
[03:40] Olivia Park: Okay that fits our org's ballpark but we need to show three-year TCO to leadership.
[03:45] Priya Kapoor: We'll include a TCO slide in the scenarios — per-token hosted costs, effective per-token after amortized dedicated costs at different utilization, plus cost savings from caching and batching.
[03:55] Mark Dalton: Any additional operational overhead with Dedicated or Private compared to Hosted? Our infra team wants minimal ops.
[04:01] Tom Reyes: For Dedicated, we manage the serving runtime and orchestration; customers configure scaling and policies. Private with a VPC control plane requires some network setup and potentially additional ops for on-prem, but we offer a managed option with Redwood handling upgrades. We'll outline operational responsibilities in the deck.
[04:17] Sarah Nguyen: About billing granularity — do you bill on tokens, or on capacity hour if dedicated?
[04:21] Priya Kapoor: Hosted is billed per token. Dedicated billing is a monthly commit for capacity, plus a small per-token overage for bursts. We provide token-level metrics so you can map chargebacks internally.
[04:31] Ethan Cole: We have a compliance requirement for audit logs and SSO; can you integrate with our Okta and provide retention for logs 12 months?
[04:38] Tom Reyes: Yes, we support SAML/Okta SSO, RBAC, and audit logs with configurable retention; for enterprise plans we can extend retention and provide SOC2/ISO artifacts. We'll attach security whitepaper and SOC2 report.
[04:50] Mark Dalton: For the benchmarking step — what do you need from us to run an apples-to-apples cost run?
[04:55] Priya Kapoor: Ideally: 1) sample prompt set representing typical calls, 2) token distribution and peak QPS windows, 3) success criteria for quality (e.g., ROUGE or business KPI), and 4) any specific models you want tested. We'll run hosted and dedicated runs and share the cost breakdown.
[05:11] Sarah Nguyen: We can export sample prompt set by EOD tomorrow.
[05:14] Olivia Park: We'll also send procurement timeline — likely decision in 6-8 weeks if the numbers look good.
[05:19] Tom Reyes: Great. One nuance on per-token math: input tokens incur encoding and attention costs but response tokens consume most of the compute budget; also model architecture affects token cost nonlinearly — so it's important we test with your actual prompts.
[05:33] Mark Dalton: Are there minimum token thresholds for volume discounts on hosted?
[05:36] Tom Reyes: Yes, discounts scale with committed monthly volume; we'll show typical breakpoints in the spreadsheet.
[05:40] Ethan Cole: If we go dedicated and later scale down, are there penalties?
[05:43] Tom Reyes: Commit terms vary. Shorter-term pilots have more flexible terms; annual commitments get better pricing. We can design a pilot commit to minimize penalties.
[05:52] Priya Kapoor: Also worth calling out caching architecture: our KV cache stores transformer KV states for recent prefixes and it's safe by default, encrypted; we can opt out per tenant. The transcript maybe transcribed as K-V cash in some exports but it's KV cache.
[06:04] Sarah Nguyen: Haha, yes heard that in other tools.
[06:06] Mark Dalton: OK, anything else on cost levers we should be aware of?
[06:09] Priya Kapoor: Model selection is huge — smaller distilled models drop cost substantially at acceptable quality for some tasks. Also mixing routing — low-latency small model for many queries, and high-quality model for high-value queries — reduces average cost.
[06:20] Olivia Park: From finance side we want a clear chart: current cost baseline, projected hosted cost, projected dedicated cost at 60/80% utilization, and breakeven month.
[06:29] Tom Reyes: We'll include breakeven calculations in the spreadsheet.
[06:32] Mark Dalton: For data residency — some clients require EU-only processing. Can Redwood route requests regionally?
[06:36] Tom Reyes: Yes, routing by region is supported; for hosted we have region controls and for private you can keep everything in VPC.
[06:42] Priya Kapoor: Quick note — we'll need a sample of long-form summarization examples to test streaming behavior and to measure token churn for caching.
[06:49] Sarah Nguyen: We'll include a set of 50 long documents.
[06:52] Tom Reyes: Perfect. Recap - action items and next steps: Tom sends pricing scenarios and security docs, Priya shares benchmark playbook, BlueHarbor provides sample prompts, token distro and procurement timeline.
[07:05] Mark Dalton: Sounds good — thanks team.
[07:08] Olivia Park: Thanks Tom and Priya.
[07:10] Tom Reyes: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
[07:13] [call ends]
